A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with matching title, authors, and central objective. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references and has no appendix; v2 includes readable supplementary Sections A–C.

before.justification: v1 reports original HOGraspNet refinement results on 300 examples in Table 1, plus qualitative reconstruction and controlled-generation results in Figures 4–5.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark comparisons, ablations, computational measurements, grasp-classification results, and supplementary HInt evaluations in Tables 1–4 and the accompanying figures.

M1.justification: v1 uses supplied ground-truth grasp labels and a text-only, CLIP-conditioned diffusion prior. v2 introduces a learned grasp classifier and replaces global text conditioning with DistilBERT text tokens, ViT image tokens, and cross-attention in AffHandGen. These substantially change the description-generation pipeline and model architecture. Occlusion-aware refinement was already present in v1.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from HOGraspNet reconstruction and text-controlled generation to HO3D and unconstrained HInt images, including New Days, VISOR, and Ego4D. v2 also evaluates grasp classification as an auxiliary task. This substantially broadens the evaluated data, environments, and task coverage.

E2.justification: v1 Table 1 compares against HaMeR and unconditional InterHandGen. v2 Table 1 adds HandOccNet, MeshGraphormer, WiLoR, Hamba, and InterHandGen with full text/image conditioning. The main InterHandGen refinement comparisons now use WiLoR initialization, substantially revising the comparison set.

E3.justification: The reported HOGraspNet evaluation expands from 300 examples to 3,000 evaluation images, and the main refinement experiments switch from HaMeR to WiLoR and Hamba. v2 adds PA-MPVPE, PCK, and mesh F-scores, alongside new HO3D and HInt protocols. The HOGraspNet S1 split and occlusion-bin definitions remain. Newly disclosed training hyperparameters are documentation additions rather than established changes to earlier settings.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's qualitative refinement and object-size controllability examples, v2 adds systematic ablations of conditioning modalities, caption generation, grasp labels, masks, encoders, guidance, and affordance fields. Figure 9 and supplementary Sections A–C add object-property analysis, classifier errors, hyperparameter sensitivity, and failure cases. The original size-control example is retained as Figure 8.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2's additional tables and sensitivity plots continue point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v1 Table 1 reports HaMeR refinement from 8.51 to 8.28 mm PA-MPJPE. Under its revised evaluation, v2 reports WiLoR refinement from 8.22 to 7.53 mm on HOGraspNet and adds HO3D results of 7.37 mm with WiLoR and 7.29 mm with Hamba. These are different experimental settings, not direct version-to-version gains. Numerous ablation, classification, efficiency, and HInt results are added; HInt includes both improvements and degradations.

T1.justification: v2 newly defines the weighted pose, vertex, and joint training objective in Equation 3, whereas v1 provides only the pose-space and conditional-denoiser formulation. This is a limited addition to mathematical specification. No new assumptions, theorems, or proofs appear; the added standard DDPM equations are explanatory.

C1.justification: The central claim that affordance descriptions improve occluded hand reconstruction and enable controllable generation is retained. v2 extends the stated contribution to learned grasp classification and joint image/text conditioning, and claims advantages over context-conditioned diffusion baselines. These refine the contribution without replacing its central research claim.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands mechanism explanations, attributing gains to token-level conditioning, modality-specific encoders, and visible-joint guidance. It interprets grasp-classification errors as having limited downstream impact. New limitations address static single-hand reconstruction, absent explicit 3D object geometry, and unreliable descriptions for unusual interactions; supplementary failure cases qualify applicability beyond training conditions.

D1.justification: v1 provides relatively few implementation details. v2 discloses loss weights, attention dimensions and heads, token counts, conditional dropout, 80 training epochs, batch size 64, Adam learning rate, scheduling, and dataset-specific refinement settings. The supplement adds classifier architecture, exact caption prompts, and post-processing settings. These materially improve reproducibility documentation without establishing that every newly disclosed setting changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds an extensive Related Work section covering hand reconstruction, affordance reasoning, and diffusion, with new works including Hamba, Text2HOI, DiffH2O, and AffordPose. It develops substantive distinctions from object-level affordance methods and globally conditioned diffusion priors, considerably expanding v1's brief introductory positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, and the method and experimental narrative are reorganized into more detailed subsections. v2 adds a standalone Related Work section, explicit limitations, and supplementary Sections A–C. These constitute substantial changes in exposition and document structure.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column formatting. Pipeline diagrams are redesigned and separated, refinement gains algorithm pseudocode, and the main results table becomes a multi-benchmark, multi-metric display. New ablation tables, heatmaps, classifier diagrams, prompts, sensitivity plots, and failure panels substantially expand visual presentation. v1 Figure 5 is retained as v2 Figure 8.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important practical weakness by replacing ground-truth grasp inputs with a learned classifier and testing predicted versus oracle labels in Table 2. Broader evaluation, a fully conditioned diffusion comparator, and component ablations substantially strengthen the evidence beyond v1's small comparison. Detailed settings and prompts also improve reproducibility. Mixed HInt outcomes and component-level timing still limit generalization and efficiency claims, but the gains in practical validity and evidential support are substantial.
